rows.basis: Sovereignty over the areas of settlement, "closest to" partial-sovereignty-area-c (rule 3); "no evidence was found for" the other elements of full-sovereignty (rule 7); caveat: adviser called the main vote a protest against the government (rule 8)

Apply sovereignty and expand settlements, no Palestinian state: full-sovereignty stated plainly (rule 3); caveat: has not said what should happen to the Palestinian Authority, Oslo or Areas A and B (rule 8)
Full sovereignty, expanding settlements and dismantling the Palestinian Authority; one option, nothing else held (rule 3)
Pre-1967 border stated plainly as first option; leader's 2024 and 2026 statements "also leave room for" one-equal-state (rule 5)
"The record matches" sovereignty over key areas only; 2022 "shrink the conflict" call and 2025 faction position "also overlap with" maintain-current-situation (rule 5)
Keep things as they are, no Palestinian state and no sovereignty; statements and record in government "both match this option" (rule 3)

Sovereignty over part of the area, here the main settlement cities (rule 3); "no evidence was found" for dismantling the Palestinian Authority, so full-sovereignty not held (rule 7); caveat: faction explained its votes as political protest (rule 8)

Keep things as they are, based on consistent votes against sovereignty bills 2023-2025, stated reason and settlement housing (rule 3); caveat: evidence on a final arrangement is "otherwise thin" (rule 8)
Sovereignty over all of Judea and Samaria and settlement expansion: full-sovereignty (rule 3); caveat: no documented position on dismantling the Palestinian Authority (rule 8)
Two states on the pre-1967 lines, all settlements evacuated, East Jerusalem as capital; rests on the 2026 Joint List position and votes since 2024 (rule 3)
No documented position found.
Sovereignty over part "or" all of the area; statements and vote support sovereignty "without saying how far" (rule 4)
Make all of Judea and Samaria part of Israel and expand settlements: full-sovereignty (rule 3); caveat: no source shows a position on dismantling the Palestinian Authority (rule 8)

Maintain-current-situation is first, backed by votes that "have not followed through"; platform and rhetoric point to full-sovereignty "or" partial-sovereignty-area-c as second element (rule 6, actions over statements)
Negotiated two states with land swaps stated plainly; shared Jerusalem capital and settlement freeze "contains elements of" two-states-pre-1967-border (rule 5)
Sovereignty over all of Judea and Samaria, expand settlements, dismantle the Palestinian Authority; one option (rule 3)
maintain-current-situation stated as closest; the line says full and partial sovereignty "cannot be confirmed or excluded", so it does not point to them as closest and they are not held
Keep the current situation, no Palestinian state, no sovereignty for now (rule 3); caveat: Sa'ar describes sovereignty as a possible later step coordinated with the United States (rule 8)
Negotiated two states; "the evidence does not say whether" land swaps keeping the blocs or the exact pre-1967 border (rule 4)

"The evidence is mixed": non-binding declaration vote "points to" partial-sovereignty-area-c (named first); votes against or absent on every binding bill are "closer to" maintain-current-situation; both sides are votes, so line order kept (rule 5)
Two states on the pre-1967 border, East Jerusalem as capital, all settlements evacuated; one option (rule 3)
Negotiated two states with the large settlement blocs staying with Israel (rule 3); caveat: rests on statements, the 2026 platform does not say "two states" or name a border (rule 8)
Sovereignty over key areas such as the Jordan Valley, "together with" continued settlement and army freedom of action, "elements of" maintain-current-situation (rule 5)

"The evidence is mixed": votes on record (Action) match partial-sovereignty-area-c, 2026 statements point to maintain-current-situation (rule 5, actions over statements); caveat: votes were cast in another party before Yashar was founded and Yashar has not said whether it holds that position

"The evidence is mixed": 2026 statements plus the vote against the comprehensive bill point to maintain-current-situation (named first); votes for Ma'ale Adumim and Jordan Valley point to partial sovereignty; 2022 stated long-term goal was separation-two-states (rule 5, third option secondary)

"The evidence is mixed": votes for sovereignty over key areas point to partial-sovereignty-area-c (named first, actions); reported 2026 remarks and list leader's position are "closer to" maintain-current-situation (rule 5, actions over statements)
Sovereignty over part of the area with full control of Area C (rule 3); caveat: gives the daily-affairs role to Jordan rather than to the Palestinians themselves (rule 8)
Make all of Judea and Samaria part of Israel, expand settlements, dismantle the Palestinian Authority; one option (rule 3)
